org.portico.utils.messaging

Class MessageSink

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.utils.messaging.AbstractMessageHandler
      • org.portico.utils.messaging.MessageSink
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    IMessageHandler

    public class MessageSink
extends AbstractMessageHandler
    A MessageSink provides a super-structure for message processing. It is the main logical unit that drives message processing in the messaging framework.

    Global Handlers

    A sink may contain any number of global IMessageHandlers. These handlers are passed every message given to the sink, regardless of message type. Global handlers are arranged as MessageChains. A global handler can be registered in one of two chains: the PREPROCESS chain or the POSTPROCESS chain. Handlers in the PREPROCESS chain are passed a message before it is given to any registered handler. Handlers in the POSTPROCESS chain are passed a message after it has been processed by its registered handler (unless the registered handler threw an exception).

    Other options for global handlers are BOTH which will see a handler added to both chains, and NONE which denotes that a handler ISN'T a global handler. This is the default stance for handlers and is needed so that the MessageHandler.global() attribute of the annotation can have a default value that says "not global".

    Registered Handlers

    Registered handlers are where the meat of the processing occurs. A handler can be registered with the sink as the handler responsible for a particular class of PorticoMessage. When requests of that class arrive, that handler is given it to process.

    The Default Handler

    If there is no registered handler for a message, it is given to the default handler. By default, the default handler is an instance of MessageSink.DefaultHandler. You can replace this with the setDefaultHandler(IMessageHandler) method.

    Handler Augmentation

    When a handler is registered, there may already be a registered handler for that same message type. In this case, the handler can be "augmented". In this case, a new MessageChain is created and the existing handler and the new handler are added to it. The chain then replaces the existing handler as the registered handler for the message type.

    If the existing message type is already a chain, the new handler is just added to the chain. NOTE: The position of handlers within a chain depends on each of their priorities. See the previous link for more information.

    If either of the handlers is marked as not augmentable, then the attempt to augment the handlers will fail and nothing will change.

    Veto Exceptions

    When a VetoException is found during processing, the sink will stop any further processing with one exception. If the exception happens in a regular handler, the global post-processing handlers will still be given the opportunity to run. If a veto happens in the global pre-processing chain, no regular or post-processing handlers will run. Before returning processing after a veto, the sink will check to see if a response message has been filled out. If one hasn't, it will automatically mark the call as a success.

    • Method Detail

      • process

        public void process(MessageContext context)
             throws Exception
        This method will trigger the processing of a message. The processing order is as follows:
        • First, all the global handlers with the role MessageSink.Global.PREPROCESS are invoked. The order depends on the relative priorities of the contained handlers.
        • Secondly, the general (or "registered") handler associated with type of the request message (its class) will be invoked. If no handler has ever been associated with this message type, it will be given to the MessageSink.DefaultHandler.
        • Finally, all the global handlers with the role MessageSink.Global.POSTPROCESS are invoked. Again, the order depends on the relative priorities of the contained handlers.
        Specified by:
        process in interface IMessageHandler
        Specified by:
        process in class AbstractMessageHandler
        Parameters:
        context - The context containing the message to process
        Throws:
        MessagingException - If there is an error or one of the handlers throws an exception

      • isAugmentable

        public boolean isAugmentable(Class<? extends PorticoMessage> forMessage)
        Returns true if there is a registered handler for the given message type. Also returns true if there is NO registered handler for the given message type (as that means it is safe to register a handler for the type). Returns false if there is an existing handler, but it is NOT augmentable.

      • setDefaultHandler

        public void setDefaultHandler(IMessageHandler defaultHandler)
        Each MessageSink has a default message handler that is passed all messages for which there is not a registered handler. This method will set the given handler as the default handler. If the given handler is null, the request is ignored.

      • registerGlobalHandler

        public void registerGlobalHandler(IMessageHandler handler,
                                  MessageSink.Global globalChain)
                           throws MessagingException
        Registers the given handler with either the global pre- or post-process MessageChain. The position of the handler within the chain depends on handlers priority compared to those of the existing handlers. If the value for globalChain is MessageSink.Global.BOTH, that handler will be added to both chains. If it is MessageSink.Global.NONE, an exception will be thrown.
        Throws:
        MessagingException

      • removeGlobalHandler

        public IMessageHandler removeGlobalHandler(String handlerName,
                                           MessageSink.Global globalChain)
        Removes and returns the first handler with the given name in the global chain identified by the given argument. If there is more than one handler of the given name, only the first is removed. If there is no handler of the given name in the chain, null is returned. If the value for globalChain is MessageSink.Global.NONE, null wil be returned.

      • getGlobalHandler

        public IMessageHandler getGlobalHandler(String handlerName,
                                        MessageSink.Global globalChain)
        Returns the first handler with the given name in the global chain identified by the given argument. If there is more than one handler of the given name, only the first is returned. If there is no handler of the given name in the chain, null is returned. If the globalChain value is MessageSink.Global.BOTH or MessageSink.Global.NONE, null will be returned.
